Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 15816 of 2020

Applicant :- Govind Vishwakarma
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Narendra Nath Tripathi,Aalok Kumar Srivastava,Ajit Manit Tripat

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.
Supplementary affidavit filed today on behalf of the applicant is taken on record.
2. Heard Sri Sanjay Tiwari, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Ravi Kant Kushwaha, learned AGA for the State.

3. The instant bail application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No. 278 of 2017, under Sections 363, 366, 376, 120B IPC and Section 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station Rampur Karkhana, District Deoria during pendency of the trial.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that this is second bail application filed on behalf of the applicant.
The first bail application of the applicant has been dismissed by this Court vide order 04.12.2019 passed in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 4612 of 2019.

sentences.text: He further submits that both the prosecutrix have already been examined by the trial court, therefore, there is no chance of tampering with the prosecution evidence.
He next submits that considering the long incarceration of applicant of about six years, applicant may be enlarged on bail.

5. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that there is allegation of rape against the applicant as applicant has taken two sisters and thereafter committed rape with one sister and after considering the entire facts of the case his first bail application was dismissed but learned AGA could not dispute the fact that applicant is in jail since 10.08.2017 i.e. for almost six years and till date trial of the case could not be concluded and even till date only three prosecution witnesses could be examined, however in the charge-sheet there are as many as 11 prosecution witnesses.
Learned AGA further could not dispute the fact that prosecutrix of the case and her sister has already examined by the trial court.
6. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

7. Although, this is second bail application filed on behalf of the applicant and first bail application of the applicant has been dismissed by this Court on merit and from the perusal of the record it also reflects that there is allegation against the applicant that he committed rape with a girl aged about 16 years but applicant in the present matter is in jail since 10.08.2017 i.e. for almost six years and till date trial of the case could not be concluded.

From the record, it further reflects that in the charge-sheet there are as many as 11 prosecution witnesses but out of them only three prosecution witnesses could be examined, therefore, it appears that trial of the case is moving with languid pace.

Further, it appears from the record that prosecutrix and her sister has already been examined by the trial court, therefore, I find force in the argument advanced by learned counsel for the applicant that as both sisters have already been examined by the trial court, therefore, there is no chance of tampering with the prosecution evidence.

8. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, particularly the long incarceration of the applicant of almost six years, in my view, applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
9. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant second bail application is allowed.

10. Let the applicant - Govind Vishwakarma be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from Govind Vishwakarma vs State Of U.P. on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142291387/
2 disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
11. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.
12.
